13 A mass of 30 kg is suspended from the end of a wire. A horizontal force F acts on the mass so
that it is in equilibrium, with the wire at an angle of 30° to the vertical, as shown.
30°
mass 30 kg
F
What is the magnitude of F ?
A
17 N
B
150 N
C
170 N
D
510 N

hints: Notice the three forces on the 30 kg mass: weight vertically down, horizontal push $F$, and tension along the wire at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical.
For equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so the horizontal and vertical components of tension must balance $F$ and $mg$ separately.
Combine $T\sin 30^{\circ} = F$ and $T\cos 30^{\circ} = mg$ to eliminate $T$ and find $F$ from the $30$ kg weight.
walkthrough: Calculate the weight of the mass: $W = mg = 30 \times 9.81 \approx 294 \text{ N}$ acting vertically down.
Let the wire tension be $T$ at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical. Resolve it: vertical component $T\cos 30^{\circ}$ up, horizontal component $T\sin 30^{\circ}$ to the left.
Apply equilibrium: vertical forces balance so $T\cos 30^{\circ} = W$, and horizontal forces balance so $T\sin 30^{\circ} = F$.
Divide the horizontal equation by the vertical equation to eliminate $T$: $F/W = \tan 30^{\circ}$, so $F = W\tan 30^{\circ}$.
Substitute values: $F \approx 294 \times 0.577 \approx 170 \text{ N}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 10. It comes from using mass $30$ instead of weight $mg$ in the force triangle.

B.explanation: Close to $W \sin 30^{\circ}$. It treats the weight as the tension in the wire, whereas the vertical component of tension balances the weight.

D.explanation: About $W / \tan 30^{\circ}$. It inverts the force triangle and divides by $\tan 30^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying.
